title: Sampling backfill + TTL mismatch scratch
content:
Goal: capture a compact timeline + commands tried for the sampling/backfill incident (Mar 11-12) — why backfilled spans are not showing up in rollup metrics and some traces missing parent links. Quick notes to self (will circulate to SRE + runtime later).

Observed behaviour:
- Backfill job launched to repopulate 2026-03-10 02:00-03:00 window. Job completed without obvious failures, but rollup metrics (span_count, trace_rate) for that window still 30–40% below expected.
- Affected traces often show a root span present but ~6–12 child spans missing; parent_id present in logging events for missing spans but those spans do not appear in tracing UI or in metrics aggregations.
- In the logs, I see many 'span dropped' lines around the same timestamp range on the ingest workers.

Key log snippets (sanitized):
- 2026-03-11T02:15:13Z obs-ingest-0 spanstore.go:214 INFO Dropped 37 spans; reason=ttl-mismatch cache_ttl=72h event_ttl=48h span_id=8f5b4e2a
- 2026-03-11T02:15:13Z obs-ingest-0 kvcache.go:89 WARN KVCache: Put failed key=svc-abc::trace-9a7b: err=stale-timestamp (write_ts=2026-03-10T02:12:03Z, min_allowed=2026-03-10T02:13:00Z)
- 2026-03-11T02:15:14Z obs-sampling-1 sampler.py:321 DEBUG Backfill worker: processing batch id=bck-20260310-0212 size=1200 hints=orig_ts
- 2026-03-11T02:15:14Z obs-sampling-1 trace-emitter.sh:45 ERROR emit failed code=412 body={"error":"span too old for ingestion window"}

Commands & queries I ran (order approximate):
- kubectl -n obs logs deploy/obs-ingest --since=2h | grep "ttl-mismatch" | head -n 40
- gcloud logging read "resource.type=container AND labels.k8s-pod=obs-sampling-1 AND textPayload:\"Backfill worker\"" --project redwood-prod --limit 1000 --order ascend
- jq to inspect backfill batches: cat backfill-output.ndjson | jq -c '{id: .batch_id, earliest: .spans[0].ts, last: .spans[-1].ts, count: .spans|length}' | head
- python tools/trace_replayer.py --input backfill-output.ndjson --target=ingest-api --dry-run (confirmed payload shapes look good)
- curl -v -X POST https://ingest.redwood.ai/v1/spans -H 'X-Env: prod' -d @sample-span.json 2>&1 | tee sample-post.log
- gcloud pubsub subscriptions pull projects/redwood-prod/subs-backfill --limit=5 --auto-ack --project=redwood-prod | jq

Reproduction attempts:
- Manually posted a small batch with original timestamps (2026-03-10T02:12:03Z) -> ingest API returned 200 but subsequent query to trace-store did not return spans.
- Same payload with timestamp bumped +1m (2026-03-10T02:13:03Z) -> accepted and visible in UI and metrics.
- Posting same spans via the backfill job pipeline (republish to pubsub) reproduced 'span too old' errors in sampling/emit logs.

Initial hypotheses (ranked):
1) TTL enforcement at KV layer: ingest pipeline has a conservative minimum-allowed-timestamp check that differs between online ingestion and backfill path (i.e., backfill respected orig_ts but downstream KV store requires ts >= min_allowed which is set from a server clock or checkpoint). Explains why bumping ts fixes it.
2) Clock skew: some backfill workers are stamping spans with original timestamps, but ingest nodes compare against local cutoff derived from last-forwarded checkpoint (checkpoint lag ~47s) and drop anything older than cutoff.
3) Sampling policy mismatch: sampler marks backfilled spans as low-priority / hint-only and the emitter has an additional TTL gate that rejects spans older than N.
4) Pub/Sub reordering + dedupe TTL: if a span delivered after a dedupe window older than dedupe TTL, it is ignored by the aggregator.

Evidence & counters:
- Clock skew: node times are within 10s across cluster (checked via kubectl exec into nodes and date +%s). Not likely >47s.
- Config differences: configmap for ingest and backfill shows INGEST_MIN_TS_OFFSET=60s and BACKFILL_ALLOW_OLD=true. But KV store has KVCACHE_MIN_AGE=90000 (which is seconds? unclear). Need to verify units: found comment 'TTL stored as hours' in kvcache code.
- Code pointer: kvcache/src/kvcache.go: Put uses compareAgainst(minAllowedFromCheckpoint()) — checkpoint calculation uses lastCheckpointTs + allowedDriftSec. That value was 60 in prod config until last week when we merged PR #389 which changed default to 3600 for dedicated clusters.

Immediate next steps (short list):
- Add logging: emit min_allowed value in kvcache Put errors so we can correlate to span timestamps (PR: obs/kvcache add context).
- Re-run small backfill with DEBUG logging and include header X-Debug-Trace: <corr> to trace end-to-end.
- Temporarily relax kvcache min_allowed in staging to match online ingestion and test backfill run.
- Search for PR #389 side effects: grep for default drifSec/TTL changes across repo.

Artifacts to dig into later:
- backfill-output.ndjson (local) + sample-post.log (attached in ticket)
- ingest-configmap-prod v.s. backfill-configmap-prod (diff)
- kvcache metrics: kv_put_failures{reason=stale-timestamp} by pod

Questions for SRE / infra folks:
- Are there any cluster-level cronjobs that rewrite timestamps on pubsub replay?
- Can we temporarily bump KVCACHE_MIN_AGE in prod canary and observe effect? What’s the safe update path?
- Is there an existing dedupe window metric we can query (dedupe_window_seconds)?

Notes to self (less formal):
- Weird that API returns 200 when emit fails later — we need stronger end-to-end success semantics for backfill path (acks from KV + metric increment)
- Consider adding a backfill-specific header so downstream can treat these writes with a different latency/ttl policy (X-Backfill-Original-Ts)
- Remember to include timeline: backfill job start 2026-03-11T01:58Z -> spike of ttl-mismatch around 02:15Z -> job finished 02:38Z but rollups low for window 02:00-03:00

Draft Slack blurb for incident channel (short):
- "Heads up: doing a targeted backfill for 03/10 02:00-03:00 window. Some spans appear to be dropped due to a TTL/min_allowed mismatch in kvcache. I'm adding debug logging + plan to run a small canary. Will update in 30m. (Ava)"

TODO (checklist):
- [ ] Add min_allowed logging in kvcache (PR)
- [ ] Run small canary backfill with DEBUG headers
- [ ] Diff configs + rollback recent PRs touching TTL defaults
- [ ] Add testcase that simulates backfill + kvcache min_allowed behavior in unit tests
- [ ] Post findings to JIRA-OBS-1789 by EOD

Timestamped breadcrumbs (for timeline):
- 2026-03-11T02:12:00Z backfill worker batch bck-20260310-0212 published to pubsub
- 2026-03-11T02:15:13Z first observed kvcache stale-timestamp errors
- 2026-03-11T02:20:30Z manual post with +1m ts showed visible trace in UI

If anyone reading: ping me on slack @ava.r with any quick ideas. Will keep this doc lean and iterate.
